raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview **Decode at c=1 on SPEED-Bench goes from 39.4 to 46.5 tok/s (+18%) with average AL unchanged (-0.4%)** with an NVFP4 draft head, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3), one DGX Spark, measured on three nodes with the SM121 skinny-GEMM plans from #59753. An MTP or EAGLE drafter that shares the target's lm_head reads the whole head once per draft token; on a 248k x 2560 BF16 head that is the largest kernel in a draft step. A new opt-in key gives the drafter a private quantized copy of the head. The target still verifies with its own BF16 head, so outputs are unchanged; only the acceptance length can move. ```bash vllm serve --speculative-config \ '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "nvfp4"}' ``` ## Claims - `"nvfp4"`: E2M1 weights with an E4M3 scale per 16 values, weight-only on the Marlin W4A16 kernel (activations stay BF16/FP16). `"fp8"`: per-row FP8 weights and per-token FP8 activations, reusing the existing online `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` on the platform FP8 kernel (`CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` on GB10). CUDA graphs and TP work (each rank quantizes its own shard). - Decode on GB10: +17.5% to +18.4% at c=1 and +9% to +11% at c=4 (NVFP4, three nodes), +10.8% / +6.5% (FP8, one node). AL within run-to-run noise, including multilingual (every row of the head stays available). GSM8K unchanged (earlier run, below). - Probabilistic drafting stays exact: the quantized logits are both sampled and used as q. - Extra memory: about 0.35 GiB (NVFP4) or 0.6 GiB (FP8) for a 248k x 2560 head, created inside model loading, so profiled KV sizing accounts for it. With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`, leave room for it. ## Validation SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories at c=1 and c=4, greedy, 256 output tokens), Flash-Next, MTP k=3, real AL from the spec-decode counters, full vocabulary. Each node ran stock and the quantized head back to back; vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with the skinny-GEMM plans of #59753 applied, plus this PR. ``` decode tok/s per user stock c=1 NVFP4 c=1 stock c=4 NVFP4 c=4 p4242-0121 39.42 46.63 (+18.3%) 26.61 29.46 (+10.7%) p4242-0547 39.45 46.69 (+18.4%) 26.54 29.44 (+10.9%) p4242-0122 39.36 46.24 (+17.5%) 26.55 28.95 (+9.0%) p4242-0122, FP8 head 43.61 (+10.8%) 28.28 (+6.5%) AL, mean of 3 nodes stock 2.670 NVFP4 2.658 (-0.4%) multilingual 2.799 / 2.845 ```
Earlier measurement, before #59753 (ABBA, larger gain) Without the skinny-GEMM plans the BF16 head GEMV is slower, so the same change measured +27%. Stock and NVFP4 ran in ABBA order (stock, nvfp4, nvfp4, stock) on one GB10 node (p4242-0073, median SM clock 2242 MHz); numbers are the mean of the two runs per arm. | vs. BF16 head | AL (avg) | AL (multilingual) | decode c=1 | decode c=1 (multilingual) | decode c=4 | step, forced AL 3, c=1 | GSM8K (256) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | BF16 head (stock) | 2.673 | 2.859 | 35.6 tok/s | 36.9 tok/s | 27.2 tok/s | 73.7 ms | 243 | | NVFP4 draft head | 2.664 (-0.3%) | 2.851 (-0.3%) | **45.2 tok/s (+27.1%)** | 46.7 tok/s (+26.7%) | 30.4 tok/s (+11.7%) | 58.2 ms | 243 | | FP8 draft head (separate node, own stock) | +0.2% | -0.6% | **+21.0%** | +19.1% | +9.7% | 61.6 ms | 247 vs 244 | The FP8 serving row comes from a second GB10 node (p4242-0067, 2496 MHz, 7G KV) against its own stock arm (36.1 tok/s c=1, AL 2.664); the forced-AL step times and GSM8K for stock and NVFP4 are from an earlier same-node run (p4242-0074, 2489 MHz). Forced AL 3, c=4 per-user step: 114.2 / 102.4 / 104.1 ms (stock / NVFP4 / FP8).
Kernel choice, draft head GEMV only (248320 x 2560, CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 x 100 replays): ``` GB200 (SM100) GB10 (SM121, M>=4) BF16 (cuBLAS) 191 to 196 us 5.50 to 5.58 ms FP8 W8A8 (selector) 111 to 113 us 2.80 to 2.84 ms <- used for "fp8" FP8 W8A16 Marlin 145 to 153 us 2.80 to 2.82 ms NVFP4 W4A16 Marlin 133 to 149 us 1.60 to 1.64 ms <- used for "nvfp4" ``` FP8 reuses the online PTPC method (platform W8A8 kernel, needs SM89+): 1.3x faster than Marlin on GB200, parity on GB10. NVFP4 calls the Marlin W4A16 kernel directly rather than going through `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel`: that selector picks a CuTe DSL kernel on GB200 that is 1.42x slower than Marlin at M=16, and its W4A4 options would need a calibrated activation scale. Independent reproduction at TP2 on 2x DGX Spark (earlier revision, MTP k=4, [#56577 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56577#issuecomment-5994233686)): +18.5% (fp8) and +19.5% (nvfp4) decode at c=1, greedy outputs byte-identical across arms. Disclaimers: - Greedy decoding on this model is not bit-reproducible run to run; per-category AL moves up to about 3% in either direction for stock as well. Across the three nodes above stock varies by 0.2% and NVFP4 by 1.0%. Absolute tok/s also varies across Spark nodes and recipes, so compare arms only within one node. - The gain shrinks with concurrency, where more tokens share each head read. ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py # all passed (GB10) pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py -k draft_lm_head # 2 passed (GB10) ```
Setup Setup: vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with #59753 applied (not in the earlier ABBA run), this PR and two Flash-Next serving prerequisites (#59309, #56273); `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ada4da32, FP8 KV cache, `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 7G` (8G in the earlier ABBA run), `--max-model-len 49152`, `--max-num-seqs 8`, MTP drafter MoE on Marlin. Every arm used the same settings.
## Details - Design: the quantization lives with the other online quantization methods, in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py`. `quantized_lm_head_copy()` builds a plain `ParallelLMHead` with that quant method and quantizes it straight from this rank's shard of the target head, so no bf16 copy is made and the target head is unchanged. FP8 reuses the existing `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`; NVFP4 adds a small weight-only Marlin method (`_LMHeadNvfp4MarlinMethod`). `ParallelLMHead` gains an optional `quant_method` argument, which `VocabParallelEmbedding` already has. - Hook: `load_eagle_model` gives the drafter that head instead of the shared target head, including the MTP per-layer `shared_head.head`. - Derived state: the copy is kept out of layerwise reload and re-derived in place from the target head whenever the target's weights are replaced (`reload_weights`, weight transfer), so sleep mode, weight reload and weight transfer keep working. During a draft-only weight update the drafter shares the target head again, as on main, and the copy is re-derived when the update finishes. - Scope: MRV2 drafters loaded through `load_eagle_model` (EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP) that share an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head running in the model dtype; other cases are rejected at config validation or load. Gemma-4 MTP is excluded because it scores a subset of its tied embedding rows directly and has no shared lm_head. DFlash and DSpark can call the same helper in a follow-up. - Not a duplicate: #56577 (Qwen4Exp only, env var, eager only) and #47584 (DSpark only, env var) add an FP8 draft head for one model or method; this is the generic version behind one config key, with CUDA graphs and NVFP4. #59740 (reduced draft vocabulary) composes with it; both add a draft-head key to `speculative_config` and hook the same place in `load_eagle_model`, so whichever lands second will reuse this quantizer for the list rows (as `draft_token_map_quantization` there) rather than add a second one. #41000, #42124 and #58343 concern heads quantized in the checkpoint, and the online quantization framework (#51285) covers linear and MoE layers but not `ParallelLMHead`. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above.
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**Reproduction on upstream main (DGX Spark, GB10)** Upstream main 02b83919aa with the heads of #59958, #59973, #59740, #60068 and #54614 merged, no other runtime patches. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP 6 with confidence stop 0.6, sparse draft head via `draft_token_map` (32k ids, 16384 dynamic rows at rank 256, `draft_token_map_quantization: nvfp4`), FP8 KV, `host_file_gather` PLE tables. SPEED-Bench throughput 2K in / 1K out, fixed OSL, c=1, n=20: | Build | tok/s/user | AL | GSM8K-256 | |---|---|---|---| | upstream main + these PRs | 49.94 | 2.68 | 249/256 | | our internal stack, same node | 49.73 | 2.65 | 245/256 | The PR route reproduces the internal stack result within noise.

nodes.body:
**fp8 `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` holds an extra copy of the head until GC runs**

On B200 with a 248320×2560 head, each fp8 refresh leaves about +0.59 GiB allocated, which is one full FP8 copy. With GC disabled, 4 refreshes in a row grow it to +2.37 GiB; `gc.collect()` brings it back to 0. nvfp4 doesn't leak.

The cause is a reference cycle. `OnlineLinearBase.create_weights` wraps `weight_loader` in `online_process_loader`, a closure that captures the layer. `replace_parameter` carries that wrapper over to the final FP8 weight, so the temporary `fresh` head from `_quantize_copy` is freed only by the cycle collector. nvfp4 avoids this because `prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin` sets a bare `Parameter`.

GC is enabled during serving, so the memory is freed eventually, but at an unpredictable time. In a "weight sync → generate" RL loop, that is up to 0.59 GiB per rank of lost headroom per sync. Either of these fixes it:
- call `gc.collect()` at the end of `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` when something was refreshed (verified, frees it all), or
- drop the wrapped `weight_loader` from the copy's parameters in `_quantize_copy`, since the copy is never loaded through a loader.
@vadiklyutiy thanks, fixed in 62f7e415ee by dropping the loader from the copy's parameters; the refresh test now asserts no allocation growth with GC disabled.

@vadiklyutiy found two more cases in draft-only weight updates, fixed in d262ddaafd:
1. A draft update writing a weight tied to the lm_head left the quantized copy stale.
2. A draft update containing `lm_head.weight` crashed, since the copy can't be loaded.

During a draft update the drafter now uses the target head, as on main; at finish the copy is restored and refreshed. No extra persistent memory. A refresh does need transient memory while re-quantizing (1.3 GiB fp8 / 4 GiB nvfp4 for a 248k x 5120 head); chunking it is an easy follow-up if needed.

Updated the baseline: the SM121 skinny-GEMM plans (#59753) merged recently and make the stock BF16 head faster on Spark. Against that baseline the NVFP4 draft head gives +17.5% to +18.4% decode at c=1 (39.4 to 46.5 tok/s, three nodes) and +9% to +11% at c=4, AL unchanged. The earlier +27% run (without #59753) is kept in the description for reference.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @stecasta.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
`ops.scaled_fp4_quant` is used. It is available for sm100+

`OnlineLinearBase.create_weights` registers the head for layerwise online processing. `quantized_lm_head_copy()` bypasses the loader, so that state is never reset. A draft weight update (`initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` on the drafter) then re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` on the already-quantized weight.
Name is too general. Might be confused
Good catch. The copy now uses the existing `ref_nvfp4_quant` instead of `scaled_fp4_quant`, so Marlin works from SM75. On GB10 the dequantized weights are identical. Fixed in 62886bbc0e.

Agreed. The copy is built once from the target head, so weight replacement would break it. It's now rejected together with weight transfer and sleep mode, and `reload_weights` raises with it. Covered by a new test. Fixed in ed4b6465f3.
Removed; replaced by the weight-replacement test. Fixed in ed4b6465f3.
Renamed to the private `_LMHeadNvfp4MarlinMethod`. Fixed in 62886bbc0e.
May we instead supports sleep mode, etc ?

I didnt support it because the quantized draft head is a copy derived once from the target head at load. Anything that replaces or restores weights afterwards leaves the copy stale or re-quantizes it.

Let me see if I can have a different approach without adding too much complexity

Found a clean way, done in e037067e9c, and the rejections are removed. The draft copy is now derived state: it's kept out of layerwise reload, and it's re-derived in place from the target head (same storage, so CUDA graphs stay valid) after `reload_weights` or a weight transfer, via `reset_lora_state`. Sleep restores it with the other draft buffers. Tested on GB10: unit tests for refresh and layerwise reload, plus an e2e that checks sleep/wake (level 1) and `reload_weights` keep outputs and AL.

Note: level 2 sleep followed by `reload_weights` drops MTP acceptance to zero on main even without this PR, because only the target is reloaded. I'll file that separately.
Correction: the level 2 issue is already tracked as #52479, with a V1 fix in #52487. I've noted there that it also affects MRV2.

@@ -74,3 +74,12 @@ vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-Base \
   is a good default to start with.
 - If your model does not support MTP, use another method such as EAGLE or draft
   model speculation.
+- When the MTP head shares the target's unquantized lm_head (most MTP models),
+  `"draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"` or `"nvfp4"` in `--speculative-config`
+  gives the drafter a quantized copy of that head (Model Runner V2). The target
+  still verifies with its own head, so outputs are unchanged; only the
+  acceptance length can move. It helps most on bandwidth-bound GPUs with a
+  large vocabulary. The copy costs about one byte (FP8) or 0.56 bytes (NVFP4)
+  per lm_head weight, e.g. 0.6 or 0.35 GiB for a 248k x 2560 head; it is
+  counted in the model weights, so with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` leave room
+  for it.

@@ -6,6 +6,11 @@
 from tests.utils import single_gpu_only
 from vllm import SamplingParams
 
+from ...utils import (
+    assert_request_outputs_match,
+    compute_acceptance_len,
+    get_test_prompts,
+)
 from .._correctness import check_mtp_correctness
 
 
@@ -37,3 +42,102 @@ def test_mtp_correctness(
         expected_accuracy_threshold,
         vllm_runner,
     )
+
+
+@single_gpu_only
+def test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    sampling_config: SamplingParams,
+    vllm_runner,
+):
+    """A quantized draft copy of the shared lm_head only changes drafting:
+    greedy outputs match stock MTP and acceptance stays within 10%."""
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", "1")
+    prompts = get_test_prompts(mm_enabled=False)
+    results = {}
+    for quant in (None, "fp8", "nvfp4"):
+        with vllm_runner(
+            "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base",
+            block_size=None,
+            enable_chunked_prefill=None,

+VOCAB, HIDDEN = 4000, 512

+def _target_head(monkeypatch, seed: int = 0) -> ParallelLMHead:
+    # Online methods read the model dtype from the current config.
+    model_config = SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online.fp8.get_current_vllm_config",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(model_config=model_config),
+    )
+    head = ParallelLMHead(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    head.weight.data.copy_(torch.randn(head.weight.shape, generator=gen) * 0.02)
+    return head.to("cuda", torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _tensors(module: torch.nn.Module) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    return dict(module.named_parameters()) | dict(module.named_buffers())
+
+
+@requires_cuda
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("quantization", "max_rel_err", "min_top1"),
+    [("fp8", 0.05, 0.9), ("nvfp4", 0.15, 0.75)],
+)
+def test_tracks_bf16_head_through_logits_processor(
+    default_vllm_config, dist_init, monkeypatch, quantization, max_rel_err, min_top1
+):
+    head = _target_head(monkeypatch)
+    target_weight = head.weight.detach().clone()
+    draft_head = quantized_lm_head_copy(head, quantization)
+
+    assert isinstance(draft_head, ParallelLMHead)
+    # The source head keeps its bf16 weight, and no bf16 copy is kept around.
+    assert torch.equal(head.weight, target_weight)
+    assert draft_head.weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+
+    logits_processor = LogitsProcessor(VOCAB)
+    hidden = torch.randn(2048, HIDDEN, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    ref = logits_processor(head, hidden).float()
+    out = logits_processor(draft_head, hidden).float()
+    assert out.shape == ref.shape == (2048, VOCAB)
+    rel_err = ((out - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item()
+    top1 = (out.argmax(-1) == ref.argmax(-1)).float().mean().item()
+    assert rel_err < max_rel_err
+    assert top1 > min_top1
+

+@requires_cuda
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("quantization", ["fp8", "nvfp4"])
+def test_refresh_follows_target_update(
+    default_vllm_config, dist_init, monkeypatch, quantization
+):
+    """After the target's weights change, the copy is re-derived in place: it
+    equals a fresh quantization of the new target, keeps its storage, and
+    frees the temporary copy without waiting for the cycle collector."""
+    head = _target_head(monkeypatch)
+    drafter = torch.nn.Module()
+    drafter.lm_head = quantized_lm_head_copy(head, quantization)
+    ptrs = {k: t.data_ptr() for k, t in _tensors(drafter.lm_head).items()}
+
+    new_weight = _target_head(monkeypatch, seed=1).weight.detach()
+    head.weight.data.copy_(new_weight)
+    gc.disable()
+    try:
+        allocated = torch.accelerator.memory_allocated()
+        refresh_quantized_lm_heads(drafter)
+        assert torch.accelerator.memory_allocated() == allocated
+    finally:
+        gc.enable()
+
+    expected = _tensors(quantized_lm_head_copy(head, quantization))
+    for name, tensor in _tensors(drafter.lm_head).items():
+        assert tensor.data_ptr() == ptrs[name]
+        if name != "workspace":
+            assert torch.equal(tensor, expected[name]), name
+    assert torch.equal(head.weight, new_weight)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Online-quantized copies of an already-loaded lm_head."""
+
+from itertools import chain
+from typing import Literal
+from weakref import WeakKeyDictionary
+
+import torch
+from torch.nn import Module, Parameter
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import UnquantizedLinearMethod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online.fp8 import (
+    Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod,
+    OnlineLinearBase,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils import (
+    marlin_make_workspace_new,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils_fp4 import (
+    apply_fp4_marlin_linear,
+    is_fp4_marlin_supported,
+    prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils import (
+    FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX,
+    ref_nvfp4_quant,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import weight_amax
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    ParallelLMHead,
+    UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.layerwise import get_layerwise_info
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import replace_parameter
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def _quantize_nvfp4(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, chunk_rows: int = 8192
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """NVFP4-quantize the rows of `weight` without the SM100+ quant kernel.
+
+    Returns packed E2M1 codes (low nibble first), E4M3 scales per 16 values and
+    the fp32 dequantization global scale, in the layout Marlin expects.
+    """
+    fp8_max = torch.finfo(torch.float8_e4m3fn).max
+    global_scale = (weight_amax(weight).float() / (FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX * fp8_max)).clamp(
+        min=1e-12
+    )
+    inv_global_scale = (1.0 / global_scale).reshape(())
+    # E2M1 magnitudes 0, 0.5, ..., 6 doubled to integers, mapped to their codes.
+    code_of = torch.zeros(13, dtype=torch.uint8, device=weight.device)
+    code_of[torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12])] = torch.arange(
+        8, dtype=torch.uint8
+    ).to(weight.device)
+    n, k = weight.shape
+    packed = torch.empty(n, k // 2, dtype=torch.uint8, device=weight.device)
+    scales = torch.empty(n, k // 16, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=weight.device)
+    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
+        rows = slice(start, start + chunk_rows)
+        values, block_scales = ref_nvfp4_quant(weight[rows], inv_global_scale, 16)
+        codes = code_of[(values.abs() * 2).long()] | ((values < 0).to(torch.uint8) << 3)
+        packed[rows] = codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)
+        scales[rows] = block_scales.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    return packed, scales, global_scale
+
+
+class _LMHeadNvfp4MarlinMethod(OnlineLinearBase):
+    """NVFP4 lm_head copy on the W4A16 Marlin kernel; activations stay in the
+    model dtype."""
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: Module) -> None:
+        packed, scales, global_scale = _quantize_nvfp4(layer.weight)
+        replace_parameter(layer, "weight", packed)
+        layer.weight_scale = Parameter(scales, requires_grad=False)
+        layer.weight_global_scale = Parameter(global_scale, requires_grad=False)
+        prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin(layer)
+        layer.register_buffer(
+            "workspace", marlin_make_workspace_new(packed.device), persistent=False
+        )
+
+    def apply(
+        self, layer: Module, x: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return apply_fp4_marlin_linear(
+            x,
+            layer.weight,
+            layer.weight_scale,
+            layer.weight_global_scale,
+            layer.workspace,
+            layer.output_size_per_partition,
+            layer.input_size_per_partition,
+            bias,
+        )
+
+
+_LM_HEAD_METHODS: dict[str, type[OnlineLinearBase]] = {
+    "fp8": Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod,
+    "nvfp4": _LMHeadNvfp4MarlinMethod,
+}
+
+
+def _quantize_copy(lm_head: ParallelLMHead, quantization: str) -> ParallelLMHead:
+    if (
+        not isinstance(
+            lm_head.quant_method, (UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
+        )
+        or getattr(lm_head, "bias", None) is not None
+        or lm_head.weight.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Quantizing an lm_head copy needs an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head "
+            "without bias."
+        )
+    if quantization == "nvfp4" and not is_fp4_marlin_supported():
+        raise ValueError(
+            "nvfp4 lm_head quantization needs a CUDA GPU with compute capability "
+            "7.5 or newer."
+        )
+    # Online methods take their output dtype from the default dtype, which is
+    # only the model dtype while the model itself is being built.
+    dtype = lm_head.weight.dtype
+    with set_default_torch_dtype(dtype):
+        head = ParallelLMHead(
+            lm_head.num_embeddings,
+            lm_head.embedding_dim,
+            params_dtype=dtype,
+            org_num_embeddings=lm_head.org_vocab_size,
+            padding_size=lm_head.padding_size,
+            prefix=lm_head.prefix,
+            disable_tp=lm_head.disable_tp,
+            quant_method=_LM_HEAD_METHODS[quantization](),
+        )
+    replace_parameter(head, "weight", lm_head.weight.data)
+    head.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(head)
+    # The copy is never loaded. The online loader wrapper captures the layer,
+    # so keeping it would leave each copy to the cycle collector.
+    for param in head.parameters(recurse=False):
+        if hasattr(param, "weight_loader"):
+            del param.weight_loader
+    return head
+
+
+# Each quantized copy maps to the head it is derived from. Weak keys, and no
+# module attribute, so the copy never owns the source as a submodule.
+_SOURCES: WeakKeyDictionary[Module, tuple[ParallelLMHead, str]] = WeakKeyDictionary()
+
+
+def quantized_lm_head_copy(
+    lm_head: ParallelLMHead, quantization: Literal["fp8", "nvfp4"]
+) -> ParallelLMHead:
+    """A ParallelLMHead holding this rank's shard of `lm_head`, quantized.
+
+    "fp8" uses per-row weight and per-token activation scales on the platform's
+    FP8 linear kernel; "nvfp4" is weight-only on Marlin. `lm_head` is left
+    unchanged and no bf16 copy of its weight is made. The copy is derived state:
+    `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` re-derives it after `lm_head` changes.
+    """
+    head = _quantize_copy(lm_head, quantization)
+    # Keep it out of layerwise reload, which would re-run
+    # process_weights_after_loading on the already-quantized weight.
+    get_layerwise_info(head).reset()
+    _SOURCES[head] = (lm_head, quantization)
+    logger.info(
+        "Quantized a %s copy of the lm_head (%d x %d per rank).",
+        quantization,
+        head.output_size_per_partition,
+        head.input_size_per_partition,
+    )
+    return head
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def refresh_quantized_lm_heads(model: Module) -> None:
+    """Re-derive the quantized lm_head copies in `model` from their source heads.
+
+    Copies in place, so CUDA graphs keep pointing at valid tensors.
+    """
+    for module in model.modules():
+        if module not in _SOURCES:
+            continue
+        fresh = _quantize_copy(*_SOURCES[module])
+        for name, tensor in chain(
+            fresh.named_parameters(recurse=False), fresh.named_buffers(recurse=False)
+        ):
+            getattr(module, name).copy_(tensor)
+
+
+# (parent, attribute, copy) for each copy swapped out by share_source_lm_heads.
+_SWAPPED: dict[Module, list[tuple[Module, str, Module]]] = {}
+
+
+def share_source_lm_heads(model: Module) -> None:
+    """Replace each quantized copy in `model` with its source head.
+
+    `model` then loads weights like a drafter sharing the unquantized head,
+    until `restore_quantized_lm_heads` swaps the copies back in.
+    """
+    swapped = [
+        (module, name, child)
+        for module in model.modules()
+        for name, child in module.named_children()
+        if child in _SOURCES
+    ]
+    for module, name, child in swapped:
+        setattr(module, name, _SOURCES[child][0])
+    _SWAPPED[model] = swapped
+
+
+def restore_quantized_lm_heads(model: Module, refresh: bool = True) -> None:
+    """Undo `share_source_lm_heads`, then re-derive the copies in `model`.
+
+    Args:
+        model: The model passed to `share_source_lm_heads`, if any.
+        refresh: Whether to re-derive the copies; False when the source heads
+            may be mid-reload.

`OnlineLinearBase.create_weights` registers the head for layerwise online processing. `quantized_lm_head_copy()` bypasses the loader, so that state is never reset. A draft weight update (`initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` on the drafter) then re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` on the already-quantized weight.
Name is too general. Might be confused
Good catch. The copy now uses the existing `ref_nvfp4_quant` instead of `scaled_fp4_quant`, so Marlin works from SM75. On GB10 the dequantized weights are identical. Fixed in 62886bbc0e.

Agreed. The copy is built once from the target head, so weight replacement would break it. It's now rejected together with weight transfer and sleep mode, and `reload_weights` raises with it. Covered by a new test. Fixed in ed4b6465f3.
Removed; replaced by the weight-replacement test. Fixed in ed4b6465f3.
Renamed to the private `_LMHeadNvfp4MarlinMethod`. Fixed in 62886bbc0e.
May we instead supports sleep mode, etc ?

I didnt support it because the quantized draft head is a copy derived once from the target head at load. Anything that replaces or restores weights afterwards leaves the copy stale or re-quantizes it.

Let me see if I can have a different approach without adding too much complexity

Found a clean way, done in e037067e9c, and the rejections are removed. The draft copy is now derived state: it's kept out of layerwise reload, and it's re-derived in place from the target head (same storage, so CUDA graphs stay valid) after `reload_weights` or a weight transfer, via `reset_lora_state`. Sleep restores it with the other draft buffers. Tested on GB10: unit tests for refresh and layerwise reload, plus an e2e that checks sleep/wake (level 1) and `reload_weights` keep outputs and AL.

Note: level 2 sleep followed by `reload_weights` drops MTP acceptance to zero on main even without this PR, because only the target is reloaded. I'll file that separately.
Correction: the level 2 issue is already tracked as #52479, with a V1 fix in #52487. I've noted there that it also affects MRV2.

issue_comments.body:
**fp8 `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` holds an extra copy of the head until GC runs**

On B200 with a 248320×2560 head, each fp8 refresh leaves about +0.59 GiB allocated, which is one full FP8 copy. With GC disabled, 4 refreshes in a row grow it to +2.37 GiB; `gc.collect()` brings it back to 0. nvfp4 doesn't leak.

The cause is a reference cycle. `OnlineLinearBase.create_weights` wraps `weight_loader` in `online_process_loader`, a closure that captures the layer. `replace_parameter` carries that wrapper over to the final FP8 weight, so the temporary `fresh` head from `_quantize_copy` is freed only by the cycle collector. nvfp4 avoids this because `prepare_fp4_layer_for_marlin` sets a bare `Parameter`.

GC is enabled during serving, so the memory is freed eventually, but at an unpredictable time. In a "weight sync → generate" RL loop, that is up to 0.59 GiB per rank of lost headroom per sync. Either of these fixes it:
- call `gc.collect()` at the end of `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` when something was refreshed (verified, frees it all), or
- drop the wrapped `weight_loader` from the copy's parameters in `_quantize_copy`, since the copy is never loaded through a loader.
@vadiklyutiy thanks, fixed in 62f7e415ee by dropping the loader from the copy's parameters; the refresh test now asserts no allocation growth with GC disabled.

@vadiklyutiy found two more cases in draft-only weight updates, fixed in d262ddaafd:
1. A draft update writing a weight tied to the lm_head left the quantized copy stale.
2. A draft update containing `lm_head.weight` crashed, since the copy can't be loaded.

During a draft update the drafter now uses the target head, as on main; at finish the copy is restored and refreshed. No extra persistent memory. A refresh does need transient memory while re-quantizing (1.3 GiB fp8 / 4 GiB nvfp4 for a 248k x 5120 head); chunking it is an easy follow-up if needed.

Updated the baseline: the SM121 skinny-GEMM plans (#59753) merged recently and make the stock BF16 head faster on Spark. Against that baseline the NVFP4 draft head gives +17.5% to +18.4% decode at c=1 (39.4 to 46.5 tok/s, three nodes) and +9% to +11% at c=4, AL unchanged. The earlier +27% run (without #59753) is kept in the description for reference.
